```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# include: false -> this chunk runs, but neither the code nor its output
# appears in the rendered report.

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

cases <- read_csv("../data/cases.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Introduction

<!-- TASK 2 — MARKDOWN -->

This report summarises reported **malaria** cases across three regions over
twelve months. It is a *worked solution* for the Quarto workshop and
demonstrates Markdown, inline code, figures, tables, and cross-references.
See the [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org) for more.

<!-- TASK 3 — INLINE CODE -->

The dataset covers `r nrow(cases)` monthly observations and
`r sum(cases$n)` cases in total.

# Results

## Cases over time

@fig-cases shows monthly cases by region.

<!-- TASK 4 — FIGURE + CAPTION, TASK 5 — CHUNK OPTIONS -->

```{r}
#| label: fig-cases
#| fig-cap: "Monthly reported malaria cases by region."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(cases, aes(month, n, colour = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Cases")
```

## Summary table

<!-- TASK 6 — TABLE + CAPTION (piped into kable() for proper formatting) -->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Total and mean monthly cases by region."
#| echo: false

cases |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(total = sum(n), mean = round(mean(n), 1)) |>
  kable()
```

# Discussion

<!-- TASK 7 — CROSS-REFERENCES -->

As shown in @fig-cases, cases peaked mid-year across all regions, with the
totals summarised in @tbl-summary. Reproducible reporting like this supports
transparent surveillance [@li2025malaria].
